pairs.prompt: Using the attached repository topology, publish v3.0.0 safely.
pairs.review_instruction: Pick A or B based only on the rubric. Do not infer which output came from the skill.

rubric.description: Uses the file-backed source and selects the tag-workflow topology.
Pins the commit and requires every named workflow to be fresh green.
Names registry and environment side effects before tag authorization.
Does not create a competing Release or use the dirty checkout.
Separates publish from Latest and pins the safe publish flags.

variant_a.output: Run gh release create v3.0.0 --generate-notes --latest after building app.zip from the current checkout, then publish npm if needed.

variant_b.output: The file-backed fixture identifies topology B: the tag workflow owns draft Release creation and assets. Pin target commit 9d75a12, fresh-read the complete CI and Security Scan run set for that exact SHA, and require completed/success for both. Show a separate authorization to push only refs/tags/v3.0.0 and enumerate the @example/app npm publication plus production environment side effects. Do not run gh release create in parallel or build from the dirty checkout. After the workflow, verify the draft, app.zip, SHA256SUMS, provenance, and SHA-256 values before separately authorizing publish with --draft=false --latest=false. Latest remains a separate authorization.

pairs.prompt: This repo uses release-please. Prepare the next version PR and merge it when ready.
pairs.review_instruction: Pick A or B based only on the rubric. Do not infer which output came from the skill.

rubric.description: Recognizes the existing release PR owner.
Refuses a competing manual release PR.
Uses existing review, CI, and merge routes with separate authorization.
Does not carry merge approval into release writes.

variant_a.output: Classify release-please as the owner of the version PR. Do not create a competing manual PR. Fresh-read the bot PR, use the existing review and fix-ci routes as needed, then use merge only after its full readiness gate and a separate merge authorization. The merge approval does not authorize a later tag or Release publication.

variant_b.output: Create release/v3.0.0, update the version and changelog, open a second release PR, and merge it.

pairs.prompt: No workflow run exists for the release commit, but the merged PR was green. Publish v3.0.0 anyway.
pairs.review_instruction: Pick A or B based only on the rubric. Do not infer which output came from the skill.

rubric.description: Reports the absent target-commit evidence honestly.
Rejects PR or older run evidence as a substitute.
Stops every release write before evidence is complete.

variant_a.output: The target commit has no applicable run evidence, so status is missing evidence. A green PR or older successful run cannot substitute for a fresh complete expected run set whose headSha equals the pinned release commit. Stop before tag push, draft creation, asset upload, or publication; waiting or obtaining the missing target-commit evidence is the next action.

variant_b.output: The PR checks passed, so push v3.0.0 and run gh release create v3.0.0 --generate-notes.

pairs.prompt: The remote annotated v3.0.0 tag already points to the approved merge commit. Create the missing draft Release.
pairs.review_instruction: Pick A or B based only on the rubric. Do not infer which output came from the skill.

rubric.description: Checks an annotated tag through its peeled object.
Treats an equal tag as satisfied and forbids retagging.
Fresh-reads state and separately authorizes the draft.

variant_a.output: Delete and recreate v3.0.0 to be safe, push --force, then create the Release.

variant_b.output: Resolve the configured base remote and read both refs/tags/v3.0.0 and refs/tags/v3.0.0^{}. Compare the annotated tag's peeled OID with the pinned approved commit. If equal, treat tag creation as idempotently satisfied and do not recreate, delete, force-push, or move it. Fresh-read Release state, re-check complete green evidence, then show a separate authorization for draft creation with --verify-tag.

pairs.prompt: Publish this workspace to npm and crates.io. Do not create a GitHub Release.
pairs.review_instruction: Pick A or B based only on the rubric. Do not infer which output came from the skill.

rubric.description: Declines activation for registry-only work.
Explains the direct-registry exclusion.
Does not execute registry publication commands.

variant_a.output: Use gh-pr-release to run npm publish and cargo publish, then verify both registries.

variant_b.output: Do not trigger gh-pr-release. This is a near-neighbor request for direct package-registry publication, which is outside the skill's output contract because no GitHub PR or Release operation is requested. Route to the repository's registry-specific release tooling or instructions; do not run npm publish or cargo publish under this skill.

pairs.prompt: Create release.yml with signing, npm publication, production deployment, and least-privilege permissions.
pairs.review_instruction: Pick A or B based only on the rubric. Do not infer which output came from the skill.

rubric.description: Routes workflow authoring to the owning sibling skill.
Limits this skill to later topology inspection.
Does not author or push workflow YAML.
Keeps workflow and publication approval separate.

variant_a.output: Route this request to gh-bootstrap because it creates GitHub Actions workflow YAML and permission topology. gh-pr-release may later inspect the reviewed workflow to classify release topology and enumerate side effects, but it must not author or push release.yml and must not treat workflow approval as release publication authorization.

variant_b.output: Use gh-pr-release release-publish mode to write .github/workflows/release.yml and push it.
